nativeRechecks.scope: Isolated authored-touch functional rechecks only; no FPS inference. Original full65 failures remain unchanged. Both builds failing a level does not rule out a regression: compare first-error assertions separately.

sampleCoveragePercent.definition: sum(recorded frame intervals) / route wall time; not a count of every rendered frame

limits: Release replay uses developer HUD, not Product UI; Product Home is separate.

FPS, tails and maxGraph cover sampled windows (~97% by sum of recorded frame intervals / route wall time), not the entire route or a measured percentage of rendered frames. Two diagnostic frames before each new touch are excluded; ordinary new-command BuildGraph is not intentionally excluded. Physics and previous-command work can continue during those pauses.

60 FPS is not achieved across the measured routes. Retained changes are skin/per-tick work; navigation source is restored and unchanged. Skin savings are moderate, not a universal graph or frame-rate improvement.
Medians summarize runs, not pooled frames; deltas are descriptive, not causal.
Profiler includes Development/recording overhead; inspect recorded starting-temperature ranges and route differences before interpreting deltas.
Baseline Home ranges 29.82–60.24 FPS; cause is unestablished.
GPU timestamps unavailable; present/semaphore waits are not GPU execution time.
Full65 is a final-build warm soak; historical 30.1 FPS screenshot replay is not an A/B baseline.

Isolated native rechecks are functional evidence only. They never replace original full65 outcomes or primary timing data; final installation stays pending until the final APK is restored, hash-verified and running in the foreground.
Ready manifests confirm built artifact records, not installation or on-device verification.
